title: PowerToys general settings lost on every restart unless manually exited from tray
summary: PowerToys general settings can be reduced to an empty settings.json after normal Windows shutdown or a graceful WM_CLOSE path, while manual tray Exit preserves the same settings, indicating a shutdown-path settings persistence race rather than startup, elevation, or antivirus interference.

status.label: Fix plan ready for design
status.detail: The report isolates a reproducible difference between manual tray Exit and session-ending/WM_CLOSE shutdown, with runner logs showing system_session_ending=true before the next launch applies empty general settings.

next_action.label: Approve shutdown-safe settings persistence design
next_action.reason: The issue includes controlled repro evidence, logs, environment details, and a replacement bug report ZIP after the automated triage rejected the first archive.

judgment.rationale: The public report supplies exact shutdown scenarios, ruled-out causes, runner log evidence, and a fresh bug report attachment. Focused source inspection shows normal startup applies general settings without saving, while apply_general_settings can save current in-memory general settings through PTSettingsHelper::save_general_settings when invoked with save=true; the shutdown-specific path needs a design that makes settings writes atomic and quiesces pending saves before session termination.
evidence: The reporter reproduced corruption after normal restart/shutdown and graceful taskkill WM_CLOSE, but not after tray icon Exit.
The reporter confirmed settings.json was already empty before relaunch when Run at startup was disabled, so the loss occurs during the previous session shutdown.
Runner logs show Runner WM_DESTROY, system_session_ending=true before the failed session and apply_general_settings: {} on the next launch.
Labels identify the area as Product-Settings and the issue has Needs-Team-Response after the author supplied a replacement bug report ZIP.

Focused source inspection found runner/main.cpp skips QuickAccessHost::stop when is_system_session_ending() is true, startup calls apply_general_settings(general_settings, false), and runner/general_settings.cpp saves general settings through PTSettingsHelper::save_general_settings when save=true.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused design to make general settings persistence shutdown-safe by separating load/apply from save, preserving the last valid settings snapshot, and synchronously flushing or suppressing writes during system-session-ending teardown.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys-owned fix is applicable because the failure affects PowerToys runner/settings persistence and the report indicates behavior differs across PowerToys exit paths rather than an external shutdown timeout or permission problem.

proposed_fixes.title: Make runner shutdown preserve the last valid General settings
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The non-manual shutdown path can race a settings save during runner teardown or session-ending handling, allowing an empty in-memory/default General settings object to be persisted over the existing settings.json. Manual tray Exit appears to take a different, safer save-then-quit path.
plan: Trace the tray Exit, WM_CLOSE, and system-session-ending code paths to identify which one invokes general settings save during teardown.

Guard PTSettingsHelper::save_general_settings for General settings so an empty/default object cannot overwrite an existing non-empty settings file unless it came from an explicit user reset or validated load.

During WM_CLOSE/WM_DESTROY with system_session_ending=true, stop scheduling asynchronous settings writes and synchronously flush any already-queued settings write before returning from the runner message loop.
Persist settings through an atomic write/replace path that keeps the previous valid settings.json if serialization or shutdown cancellation fails.
Add regression coverage that simulates session-ending/WM_CLOSE teardown with pending General settings changes and verifies existing module enablement and enable_quick_access are preserved.
verification: Reproduce issue #50616 by changing General/module settings, restarting Windows without tray Exit, and confirming settings.json is not reduced to {}.
Repeat the graceful taskkill /IM PowerToys.exe scenario and confirm General settings persist.
Run focused runner/settings unit tests for guarded General settings saves and atomic write fallback.
Smoke test manual tray Exit to confirm the existing successful path is unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The report strongly isolates the shutdown path and source inspection identifies relevant load/save boundaries, but the exact async writer or teardown callback needs a focused design pass before implementation.

issue_context.summary: A detailed report shows General settings are lost across normal shutdown/restart and graceful WM_CLOSE, but not when PowerToys is manually exited from the tray.
known_information: PowerToys version v0.101.2362 Stable; reproduced with WinGet and both elevated and non-elevated launches.
The reporter increased Windows shutdown timeouts, disabled run-at-startup, tested both installation scopes, and ruled out obvious AV/EDR interference.
The reporter supplied a replacement PowerToysReport ZIP after automated triage rejected the first attachment.
Runner logs distinguish a failing session-ending close from a successful manual restart/exit path.
inferences: The problem is more likely a PowerToys teardown/settings-write race than a Windows shutdown timeout.
Manual tray Exit likely follows a distinct path that quiesces or orders settings persistence more safely than WM_CLOSE/session-ending.
A code fix should preserve existing settings on invalid/empty shutdown writes rather than ask the reporter for more diagnostics first.
issue_context.analysis: The report already contains the discriminating evidence needed for a design gate: precise close paths, controlled negative tests, and logs showing when the empty settings are applied. The next useful maintainer action is a focused design for shutdown-safe settings writes and regression tests.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the public issue body, author follow-up, labels, automated triage comment, and replacement attachment metadata.
Searched related open issues for settings.json shutdown and found only this issue.
Inspected runner/main.cpp around startup and teardown and runner/general_settings.cpp around General settings save behavior.

actions.label: Approve shutdown-safe settings persistence design

design.title: Make General settings persistence safe during shutdown and WM_CLOSE
design.prompt: Design a focused fix for PowerToys issue #50616. Use the public evidence that normal Windows shutdown and graceful WM_CLOSE can leave settings.json as {}, while tray Exit preserves settings. Trace the runner tray-exit, WM_CLOSE, and system_session_ending teardown paths; prevent empty/default General settings snapshots from overwriting an existing valid settings file; synchronously flush or suppress pending saves during session-ending; use atomic write/replace semantics; and add regression coverage for shutdown/WM_CLOSE persistence without changing the successful tray Exit behavior.

actions.note: Approval starts fork-side design/implementation work only; no upstream write occurs automatically.

reproduce.version_requirement: v0.101.2362 or a current build before the shutdown-persistence fix
prerequisites: PowerToys installed with General settings changed from defaults
Run at startup can be disabled for the before-relaunch check
steps: Change at least one General setting and one module enabled/disabled state.
Restart or shut down Windows without using tray icon Exit.
Before relaunching PowerToys, inspect %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\settings.json if Run at startup was disabled.
Launch PowerToys and inspect runner logs for apply_general_settings and module enablement.
Repeat with tray icon Exit as the control path.
reproduce.expected_result: settings.json remains a populated valid General settings file and module enablement persists after shutdown/WM_CLOSE exactly as after tray Exit.

upstream_safety.detail: No comments, labels, assignments, closures, or other public mutations were made to microsoft/PowerToys.
